Subject: Intro: Prompt telemetry & Redwood - initial ask

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking a look — I lead integrations at PromptLab and we build tooling around prompt testing and telemetry for ISVs and consultancies. We're evaluating partners to provide a standardized tracing/telemetry path for prompt-level events across LangChain/LlamaIndex SDKs and related wrappers.

High-level ask: we want to work with Redwood to define a "conformance kit" that lets PromptLab customers (and third-party SDKs) validate their telemetry is compatible with Redwood tracing, batching metadata, and prompt-level metrics.

Can you share:
- A short scoping template or sample SOW we can review
- Any requirements around PII/HIPAA for telemetry payloads (some of our healthcare customers ask)
- Examples of the trace context headers/fields Redwood expects (or a small spec)

I've attached a brief proposal that explains how PromptLab captures prompt prompts/variants, evaluation results, and anonymized token metadata.

Attachment: promptlab-telemetry-proposal.pdf (pdf)

Would love to schedule a quick 30 min call to scope — next week works for us.

Thanks,
Olivia

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Intro: Prompt telemetry & Redwood - initial ask

Hi all — adding a few technical bullets so we have something concrete to discuss on the call. These are based on our recent SDK partner work.

Minimum expectations for the conformance kit:
- Trace context: support W3C traceparent/ tracestate headers and our optional x-rw-request-id header for request-level attribution.
- Prompt-level events: include an event type (prompt.request / prompt.response / eval.result), a stable prompt_id, variant_id, model_name, token_count, and elapsed_ms.
- KV cache markers: if the SDK supplies cache hits, include cache_hit=true/false and cache_ttl_ms as metadata.
- Batching metadata: batch_id and position_in_batch (0..N-1) so we can reconstruct per-token ordering.
- Sampling: include a sampling_rate field if events are downsampled.

Suggested deliverables in the kit:
- A small reference shim (python/js) that maps PromptLab's capture schema to Redwood's expected fields.
- A CSV checklist used by QA teams (I attached an example).
- A validation harness that can replay sample traces and assert conformance rules.

I've attached a quick telemetry-checklist.csv you can pre-fill with one or two sample traces. We'll review these during the call and use them to produce the tech spec.

Attachment: telemetry-checklist.csv (csv)

On the HIPAA note — the main ask will be to ensure no raw PHI is serialized in telemetry. If PromptLab wants a formal attestation we can add language to the SOW that specifies allowable fields and hashing/pseudonymization steps.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Inference Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
